(Ord. No. 1.1, § 2(2.2), 4-13-98)
1127:
(a) No extension or addition to the city's public sewers intended to serve more than one (1) user shall be constructed, accepted for city ownership, or connected to the POTW until:
(1) Reports, plans, and specifications have been prepared by, or under the direct supervision of, and the construction is executed under the direct supervision of, a registered professional engineer;
(2) The applicable reports, plans, and specifications have been submitted to and accepted by the director;
(3) As-constructed plans, reports of testing and inspection, and other data required by the director have been submitted to and accepted by the director; and
(4) All permits, licenses and approvals required by federal, state, city and other local ordinances have been obtained.
(b) For each extension or addition to the city's public sewers, the city building official shall maintain a permanent record of the building permit application and issuance thereon, which record shall indicate the name of the developer, contractor and professional engineer of record pursuant thereto.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 2(2.3), 4-13-98)
1128:
(a) No person shall uncover, make any connections with or opening into, use, alter, or disturb any public sewer or appurtenance thereof without first obtaining a written permit from the city building official.
(b) There shall be two (2) classes of building sewer permits: (1) residential and/or commercial service, and (2) service to establishments producing industrial wastes. In either case, the owner or an agent thereof shall make application on a form furnished by the city. The permit application shall be supplemented by any plans, specifications or other information required by the city building official. Permit and inspection fees shall be paid to the city when the application is filed in accordance with a rate schedule adopted by the city council from time to time and made available to the public at the office of the city manager.
(c) No costs and expenses incident to the installation and connection of a building sewer from the building to the property line shall be borne by city. The user shall indemnify the city from any loss or damage that may directly or indirectly be occasioned by the installation of the building sewer.
(d) A separate and independent building sewer shall be provided for each building. Where a building stands to the rear of another on a single lot and no private sewer is available or can be constructed to the rear building through an adjoining alley, courtyard, or driveway, the city may grant permission for the building sewer from the front building to be extended to the rear building and the whole considered as one (1) building sewer, upon a showing by the applicant that it is not feasible that the two (2) buildings so connected will ultimately be on separate building lots.
(e) Existing, previously approved building sewers may be used in connection with new buildings only when found by the city building official, upon examination and testing at no cost to the city, to meet all the requirements of this section.
(f) The design, size, slope, alignment, materials of construction of a building sewer, and the methods used in excavating, placing of the pipe, jointing, testing, and backfilling the trench, shall all conform to the requirements of the city's approved building and plumbing codes. In the absence of code provisions or amplification thereof, the materials and procedures set forth in the WEF Manual of Practice No. FD-5 shall apply.
(g) Whenever possible, the building sewer shall be brought to the building at an elevation below the basement or first floor. No building sewer shall be made parallel to or within three (3) feet of any bearing wall which might thereby be weakened. The depth shall be sufficient to afford protection from live loads which may be superimposed. The building sewer shall be made at uniform grade and in straight alignment. The building sewer shall be constructed to that point of connection as directed by the city building official.
(h) No person shall maintain or make a connection of roof down spout, exterior foundation or sub-surface drains, area-way drains, or other sources of surface runoff or ground water to a building sewer or building drain.
(i) Before any underground portions thereof are covered, the applicant for the building sewer permit shall notify the city when the building sewer is ready for inspection and connection to the public sewer. All connections to the public sewers shall be conducted under the supervision of an authorized representative of the city.
(j) All excavations for building sewer installations shall be adequately guarded with barricades and lights so as to protect the public from hazards. Streets, sidewalks, parkways, and all other public property disturbed in the course of the work shall be restored in a manner satisfactory to the city.
(k) The director shall keep a permanent and accurate record of the location, depth, and direction of all new sewer connections including any landmarks as may be necessary to make an adequate description.
(l) Grease, oil, and sand interceptors shall be provided when, in the opinion of the director, they are necessary for the proper handling of liquid wastes containing oil or grease in excessive amounts or any flammable wastes, sand or other harmful ingredients, except that such interceptors shall not be required for private, single-family living quarters or dwelling units. All interceptors shall be of a type and capacity approved by the director and shall be located so as to be readily and easily accessible for cleaning and inspection. All interceptors shall be supplied and properly maintained continuously in satisfactory and effective operation by the owner at owner's expense.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 2(2.4), 4-13-98)

1131:
The categorical pretreatment standards found at 40 CFR Chapter I, Subchapter N, Parts 405-471 are hereby incorporated.
(a) Where a categorical pretreatment standard is expressed only in terms of either the mass or the concentration of a pollutant in wastewater, the city may impose equivalent concentration or mass limits in accordance with 40 CFR 403.6(c).
(b) When wastewater subject to a categorical pretreatment standard is mixed with wastewater not regulated by the same standard, the city shall impose an alternate limit using the combined waste stream formula in 40 CFR 403.6(e).
(c) An industrial user may obtain a variance from a categorical pretreatment standard if the industrial user can prove, pursuant to the procedural and substantive provisions in 40 CFR 403.13, that factors relating to its discharge are fundamentally different from the factors considered by EPA when developing the categorical pretreatment standard.
(d) A significant industrial user may obtain a net gross adjustment to a categorical standard in accordance with 40 CFR 403.15.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 2(2.7), 4-13-98)
1132:
The city reserves the right to establish, by ordinance or in wastewater discharge permits, more stringent standards or requirements than set forth herein above.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 2(2.8), 4-13-98)
1133:
No industrial user shall increase the use of process water, add cooling water, or in any way attempt to dilute a discharge, as a partial or complete substitute for adequate treatment to achieve compliance with a discharge limitation unless expressly authorized by an applicable pretreatment standard or requirement. The director may impose mass limitations on industrial users who are using dilution to meet applicable pretreatment standards or requirements, or in other cases when the imposition of mass limitations is appropriate.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 2(2.9), 4-13-98)
1135:
Industrial users shall provide wastewater treatment as necessary to comply with this article and shall achieve compliance with all categorical pretreatment standards, local limits, and the prohibitions set out in section 21-119, section 21-120, and (if applicable) section 21-121 of this article within the time limitations specified by EPA, the state, or the city. Any facilities necessary for compliance shall be provided, operated, and maintained at the industrial user's expense. Detailed plans describing such facilities and operating procedures shall be submitted to the city for review, and shall be acceptable to the city before such facilities are constructed. The review of such plans and operating procedures shall in no way relieve the industrial user from the responsibility of modifying such facilities as necessary to produce a discharge acceptable to the city under the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 3(3.1), 4-13-98)
1136:
(a) Whenever deemed necessary, the city may require an industrial user to install a monitoring manhole and/or flow measuring flume, to restrict their discharge during peak flow periods, to discharge certain wastewaters only into specific sewers, to relocate and/or consolidate points of discharge, to separate sewage waste streams from industrial waste streams, and take such other actions as may be necessary to protect the POTW and demonstrate the industrial user's compliance with the requirements of this article.
(b) The city may require any person discharging into the POTW to install and maintain, on their property and at their expense, suitable storage and flow-control facilities to ensure equalization of flow. A wastewater discharge permit may be issued solely for flow equalization.
(c) Industrial users with the potential to accidentally discharge flammable substances may be required to install and maintain an approved combustible gas detection meter.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 3(3.2), 4-13-98)
1138:
(a) Hauled wastewater may be introduced into the POTW only at locations designated by the city and at such times as are established by the director. Such wastewater shall not violate any requirement of section 21-119 or section 21-120 of this article, or any other requirements established by the city.
(b) Persons proposing to discharge hauled wastewater into the POTW shall apply for and obtain wastewater discharge permits prior to discharge. The city may require generators of hauled industrial waste to obtain wastewater discharge permits. The city reserves the right to prohibit the disposal of any hauled wastewater into the public sewers or treatment facilities. The discharge of hauled wastewater shall be subject to all other requirements of this article, including specifically the prohibited discharge standards and local limits.
(c) Septic tank and industrial waste haulers shall discharge loads only at locations designated by the director and no hauled wastewater shall be discharged without prior consent of the director. The director may collect samples of each hauled wastewater load to ensure compliance with applicable requirements of this article. The director may require any waste hauler to provide a waste analysis of any load prior to discharge. All costs of such sample collection and analysis shall be at no expense to the city.
(d) Industrial waste haulers shall provide a waste-tracking form for every load, with this form including at least, at a minimum, the name and address of the industrial waste hauler, permit number, truck identification, names and addresses of sources of waste, and volume and characteristics of waste. The form shall identify the type of industry, and all known or suspected waste constituents.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 3(3.4), 4-13-98)
1140:
When requested by the director, an industrial user shall submit, within ninety (90) days of the request, information on the nature and characteristics of its wastewater. The director is authorized to prepare a form for this purpose and may periodically require industrial users to update this information.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 4(4.1), 4-13-98)
1141:
(a) No significant industrial user shall discharge wastewater into the POTW without first obtaining a wastewater discharge permit from the city, except that any significant industrial user holding a valid wastewater discharge permit on the effective date of this article may continue to discharge for the time period specified within the wastewater discharge permit.
(b) The city may require other industrial user's to obtain other permits as necessary to carry out the purposes of this article.
(c) Any violation the terms and conditions of a wastewater discharge permit shall be deemed a violation of this article and shall subject the permittee to the sanctions set out in sections 21-140.7 through 21-140.31 of this article. Holding a wastewater discharge permit does not relieve a permittee of its obligation to comply with all federal and state pretreatment standards or requirements or with any other requirements of federal, state, and local law.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 4(4.2), 4-13-98)
1142:
Any industrial user required to obtain a wastewater discharge permit who was discharging wastewater into the POTW prior to the effective date of this article and who wishes to continue such discharges in the future, shall, within ninety (90) days after said date, notify the director of intent to continue discharge under the existing wastewater discharge permit.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 4(4.3), 4-13-98)
1143:
Any industrial user required to obtain a wastewater discharge permit who proposes to begin or recommence discharging into the POTW shall obtain such wastewater discharge permit prior to the beginning or recommencing of such discharge. An application for this wastewater discharge permit, in accordance with section 21-132 of this article, shall be filed at least ninety (90) days prior to the date upon which any discharge will begin or recommence.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 4(4.4), 4-13-98)
1145:
Wastewater discharge permit applications and user reports shall be signed by an authorized representative of the user and contain the following certification statement:
"I certify under penalty of law that this document and all attachments were prepared under my direction or supervision in accordance with a system designed to assure that qualified personnel properly gather and evaluate the information submitted. Based on my inquiry of the person or persons who manage the system, or those persons directly responsible for gathering the information, the information submitted is, to the best of my knowledge and belief, true, accurate, and complete. I am aware that there are significant penalties for submitting false information, including the possibility of fine and imprisonment for knowing violations."
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 4(4.6), 4-13-98)
1146:
The director will evaluate the wastewater discharge permit application and data furnished by the applicant and will, within forty-five (45) days of receipt of a complete wastewater discharge permit application, determine whether or not to issue a wastewater discharge permit. The director may deny any application for a wastewater discharge permit.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 4(4.7), 4-13-98)
1148:
A wastewater discharge permit shall be issued for a specified time period, not to exceed three (3) years from the effective date of the permit. A wastewater discharge permit may be issued for a period less than three (3) years, at the discretion of the director. Each wastewater discharge permit shall indicate a specific date upon which it will expire.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 5(5.1), 4-13-98)
1150:
The director shall provide public notice of the issuance of a wastewater discharge permit. Any person, including the permittee, may petition the director to reconsider the terms of a wastewater discharge permit within thirty (30) days of notice of its issuance.
(a) Failure to submit a timely petition for review shall be deemed to be a waiver of the administrative appeal.
(b) In its petition, the appealing party must indicate the wastewater discharge permit provisions objected to, the reasons for this objection, and the alternative condition, if any, it seeks to place in the wastewater discharge permit.
(c) The effectiveness of the wastewater discharge permit shall not be stayed pending the appeal.
(d) If the director fails to act within thirty (30) days, a request for reconsideration shall be deemed to be denied. Decisions not to reconsider a wastewater discharge permit, not to issue a wastewater discharge permit, or not to modify a wastewater discharge permit shall be considered final administrative actions for purposes of judicial review.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 5(5.3), 4-13-98)
1152:
Wastewater discharge permits shall not be transferred to new owners or operators.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 5(5.5), 4-13-98)
1154:
An industrial user with an expiring wastewater discharge permit shall, not later than ninety (90) days prior to the expiration of the industrial user's existing wastewater discharge permit, apply for wastewater discharge permit reissuance by submitting a complete permit application, in accordance with section 21-132 of this article.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 5(5.7), 4-13-98)
1156:
(a) Within either one hundred eighty (180) days after the effective date of a categorical pretreatment standard, or the final administrative decision on a category determination under 40 CFR 403.6(a)(4), whichever is later, existing categorical standard users currently discharging to, or scheduled to discharge to, the POTW shall submit to the director a report which contains the information listed in subsection (b), below. At least ninety (90) days prior to commencement of their discharge, new sources, and sources that become categorical standard users subsequent to the promulgation of an applicable categorical standard, shall submit to the director a report which contains the information listed in subsection (b)(1)—(5), below. A new source shall report the method of pretreatment it intends to use to meet applicable categorical standards. A new source also shall give estimates of its anticipated flow and quantity of pollutants to be discharged.
(b) Industrial users described above shall submit the information set forth below.
(1) Identifying information. The name and address of the facility, including the name of the operator and owner.
(2) Environmental permits. A list of any environmental control permits held by or for the facility.
(3) Description of operations. A brief description of the nature, average rate of production, and standard industrial classifications of the operation(s) carried out by such industrial user. This description should include a schematic process diagram which indicates points of discharge to the POTW from the regulated processes.
(4) Flow measurement. Information showing the measured average daily and maximum daily flow, in gallons per day, to the POTW from regulated process streams and other streams, as necessary, to allow use of the combined waste stream formula set out in 40 CFR 403.6(e).
(5) Measurement of pollutants.
a. The categorical pretreatment standards applicable to each regulated process.
b. The results of sampling and analysis identifying the nature and concentration, and/or mass, where required by the standard or by the director of regulated pollutants in the discharge from each regulated process. Instantaneous, daily maximum, and long-term average concentrations, or mass, where required, shall be reported. The sample shall be representative of daily operations and shall be analyzed in accordance with procedures set out in section 21-140.9 of this article.
c. Sampling must be performed in accordance with procedures set out in section 21-140.10 of this article.
(6) Certification. A statement, reviewed by the industrial user's authorized representative and certified by a professional engineer registered in Georgia, indicating whether pretreatment standards are being met on a consistent basis, and, if not, whether additional operation and maintenance and/or additional pretreatment is required to meet the pretreatment standards and requirements.
(7) Compliance schedule. If additional pretreatment and/or operations or maintenance will be required to meet the pretreatment standards, the shortest schedule by which the industrial user will provide such additional pretreatment and/or operations and maintenance. The completion date in this schedule shall not be later than the compliance date established for the applicable pretreatment standard. A compliance schedule pursuant to this section must meet the requirements set out in section 21-140.3 of this article.
(8) Signature and certification. All baseline monitoring reports must be signed and certified in accordance with section 21-133 of this article.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 6(6.1), 4-13-98)
1158:
Within ninety (90) days following the date for final compliance with applicable categorical pretreatment standards, or in the case of a new source following commencement of the introduction of wastewater into the POTW, any industrial user subject to such pretreatment standards and requirements shall submit to the director a report containing the information described in section 21-140.2(b)(4)—(6) of this article. For industrial users subject to equivalent mass or concentration limits established in accordance with the procedures in 40 CFR 403.6(c), this report shall contain a reasonable measure of the industrial user's long-term production rate. For all other users subject to categorical pretreatment standards expressed in terms of allowable pollutant discharge per unit of production (or other measure of operation), this report shall include the user's actual production during the appropriate sampling period. All compliance reports must be signed and certified in accordance with section 21-133 of this article.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 6(6.3), 4-13-98)
1159:
The city may sample and analyze any industrial user's discharges in lieu of requiring the industrial user to conduct self-monitoring sampling, analysis, and compliance reporting.
(a) The director may require any industrial user, at a frequency determined by the director, to submit periodic compliance reports indicating the nature and concentration of pollutants in the discharge which are limited by pretreatment standards and the measured or estimated average and maximum daily flows for the reporting period. All periodic compliance reports shall be signed and certified in accordance with section 21-133 of this article.
(b) All wastewater samples shall be representative of the industrial user's discharge. Wastewater monitoring and flow measurement facilities shall be properly operated, kept clean, and maintained in good working order at all times. The failure of an industrial user to keep monitoring facilities in good working order shall not be was for the industrial user to claim that sample results are unrepresentative of its discharge.
(c) If any industrial user subject to the reporting requirement in this section monitors any pollutant more frequently than required by the director, using the procedures prescribed in section 21-140.9 of this article, the results of this monitoring shall be included in the report.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 6(6.4), 4-13-98)
1160:
Industrial users shall notify the director of any planned significant changes to the industrial user's operations or system which might alter the nature, quality, or volume of its wastewater at least thirty (30) days before the change.
(a) The director may require the industrial user to submit such information as may be deemed necessary to evaluate the changed condition, including the submission of a wastewater discharge permit application under section 21-132 of this article.
(b) The director may issue a wastewater discharge permit under section 21-134 of this article or modify an existing wastewater discharge permit under section 21-138 of this article in response to changed conditions or anticipated changed conditions.
(c) For purposes of this requirement, significant changes include, but are not limited to, flow increases of twenty (20) percent or greater, and the discharge of any previously unreported pollutants.
(Ord. No. 1.1, § 6(6.5), 4-13-98)
1161:
(a) In the case of any discharge, including, but not limited to, accidental discharges, discharges of a nonroutine, episodic nature, a noncustomary batch discharge, or a slug load, that could create pass through or interference at the POTW, the industrial user shall immediately telephone and notify the director of the incident. 1199:
This article described two (2) related policies of the city for the management of the city water system. First is the drought contingency plan for temporary implementation during a water shortage emergency. The second is LaFayette's Water Conservation Plan, a program of policies for long-range conservation of water.
The purpose of LaFayette's Drought Contingency Plan ("plan") is to provide guidelines for the city to follow in the event of water shortage emergencies. The plan establishes priorities of water use and provides for allocation of available water during four (4) stages of water shortage, in increasing order of severity of the shortage.
Conditions that could cause implementation of the plan could be anything that causes a decrease in water availability from the city water facilities, such as failure of one (1) or more pumps, prolonged power outage, control malfunction, or water main breaks, sudden increases in water demand because of fire emergencies, excessive heat, cold, or drought. When demand for water exceeds the city's water system's capacity, action must be taken to prevent serious shortages and disruption of water service and fire protection to the customers. In a growing community, such as in Lafayette and Walker County, it is probable that the growth in water demand may sometimes exceed the water system's capacity to produce water. Problems and delays could arise in obtaining and developing sufficient sources of water, in financing and constructing needed treatment facilities, pumping stations, storage tanks, and distribution pipes, etc. Even with the best planning and construction, it is not considered economically feasible to provide excess capacity for every possible contingency, for excessive growth, or for every drought.
While the plan is intended to deal with short-term shortages that may occur from time to time, the plan is a program of policies adopted by the city to promote long-term efficient use and conservation of the water resources available to the city and Walker County, thus minimizing the frequency and duration of emergency water shortages.
(Ord. No. 01-2, § 1, 1-8-2001)

(a) Water use priorities a general ranking of priority water uses in decreasing order of importance are to be as follows:
(1) Household use.
(2) Public necessity.
(3) Livestock.
(4) Industry and commercial use.
(5) Construction.
(6) Irrigation.
(7) Nonessential fire fighting.
(8) Swimming pools.
(9) Car washing.
(10) Street cleaning, line flushing, hydrant testing, etc.
(b) Implementing the drought contingency plan. Implementing the plan will be contingent upon numerous interrelated factors that may cause a temporary shortage of water. In general, any event or series of events which disrupts, or threatens to disrupt the city's water supply and distribution system will be carefully evaluated and the appropriate stage of the plan will be implemented in response. In certain cases, the Georgia Environmental Protection Division (EPD) may order the plan to be implemented whether or not the city has acted.
(c) Implementation stages. The plan will be implemented in four (4) stages, depending on the severity of the water shortage. Each stage has specific goals for reducing water consumption.
Stage No. 1—Minor water emergency
The city will, when minor conditions occur, first put the following priority conservation methods in place. Under minor conditions when a request is made hereunder by the city manager, compliance shall be on a voluntary basis.
• Public service announcements will be made on local radio stations and in the newspaper requesting that customers curtail the use of unnecessary water in watering lawns and gardens, washing cars, and other practices that are not essential during emergency conditions.
• Fire departments and others will be asked to curtail water main flushing, dust control, and other nonessential use of water.
Stage No. 2—Moderate water emergency
If water shortages continue, such that up to fifteen (15) percent to eighteen (18) percent reduction in water use is deemed necessary, the city will declare a moderate water emergency condition and will take the following additional actions:
• Make additional news releases to the news media and advise of the increased intensity of the water shortage by explaining the degree of severity of the water shortage problem and the need for additional curtailment of water use.
• Make additional and more urgent appeals to all customers, especially the significant industrial users, for additional voluntary reductions of water use with a goal of eighteen (18) percent reduction.
• Use city employees to read meters of significant industrial users to gauge the extent of their water reduction.
• Use city employees and law enforcement agencies to monitor outdoor use of water by all customers.
• Prohibit all outdoor use of water for car washing (except at commercial facilities), watering lawns, garden and landscape watering, pavement hosing, and filling swimming pools 9:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m.
• Water customers observed using water in violation of Stage No. 2 restrictions will be warned by the city and requested to comply with the plan. If after one (1) such warning and request, the customer fails to comply, then the customer's water service will be cut off at the meter and a reconnection fee of one hundred dollars ($100.00) will be charged to return the customer to service. If said service is cut off and then reconnected, any additional violation of Stage No. 2 restrictions by said customer will cause the city to cut off service at the meter until emergency water shortage conditions have improved to the point where Stage No. 2 restrictions are lifted by the city and a reconnection fee of one hundred dollars ($100.00) will be charged to return the customer to service.
Stage No. 3—Severe water emergency
In cases where up to thirty (30) percent reduction in water use is deemed necessary, the city will declare a severe water emergency condition and may add the following actions:
• Notify the news media that a severe water emergency has been declared and request cooperation in reaching all water customers with the need to further curtail water use.
• Hand deliver letters to individual large water users outlining the severity of the problem and requesting significant voluntary curtailment of water use. Industrial users will be requested to reduce average consumption by at least thirty (30) percent of their normal use and advised that city employees will read water meters to monitor the level of reduction achieved.
• Prohibit all water usage by governmental agencies not required for health and safety.
• Prohibit all outside water usage at all times by all customers except that water use which is essential or required for health or safety.
• Prohibit all once-through cooling water use or water-cooled air-conditioners with recirculation.
• Prohibit the escape of water through breaks or excessive leaks in plumbing facilities by cutoff of the water service of offending customers.
• Require commercial car washing and commercial laundries to reduce water use up to fifty (50) percent of normal use as demonstrated by meter readings.
• If a water customer violates the Stage No. 3 restrictions, after one (1) request is made of the customer for compliance, the customer's water service will be cut off and a reconnection fee of two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) will be charged to return the customer to service. If said service is cut off and then reconnected, any other violation of Stage No. 3 restrictions by said customer will cause the city to cut off service at the meter until the emergency water shortage conditions have unproved to the point where Stage No. 3 restrictions are lifted by the city. A reconnection fee of two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) will be charged to return the customer to service.
Stage No. 4—Critical water emergency
If a water shortage emergency becomes so severe that it is declared critical water emergency and a fifty (50) percent or greater reduction is deemed necessary, the city will add the following additional actions:
• Additional prohibitions will be imposed on the use of any water activities not essential or required for health and safety.
• After twenty-four-hour notice to industrial users, the flow of water to the users will be shut off or reduced to the absolute minimum necessary to protect health and safety.
• Prohibit all water use for commercial car washing, commercial laundries, construction activities, and irrigation for agriculture.
• Notify all water customers that any water use greater than their average monthly use (on an annual basis) will be penalized by a fine of two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) per month until the emergency has subsided.
• The city may also issue any other requirements to reduce water use in other specific ways, using the priority list herein as a guide to the degree of curtailment.
• All city personnel will monitor unnecessary use of water and report violations of Stage No. 4 restrictions.
• Upon a customer's first violation of Stage No. 4 restrictions, the customer's water will be discontinued, upon notification to the customer, until the water shortage conditions have improved to the point where the city lifts Stage No. 4 restrictions. A reconnection fee of five hundred dollars ($500.00) will be charged to return the customer's service.
(Ord. No. 01-2, § 1, 1-8-2001)

(a) Management of water system losses. EPD guidelines recommend that system losses be reduced to ten (10) percent or less. The city is currently attempting to minimize unaccounted water use and it is evident that continuing efforts will be needed to bring the water losses within acceptable limits.
Typically, water system losses are the result of system leaks, line breaks, unmetered sales, uncalibrated or faulty meters, and unmetered uses such as fire hydrant use and line flushing. Sometimes the water is allowed to bleed off in certain locations during cold weather to prevent freezing.
The following policies will be initiated by the city to ensure that the water system returns to an acceptable water loss ratio:
• All distribution system leaks will be repaired as quickly as possible. City employees, including members of fire and police departments, are trained to report any water line leaks or breaks.
• Best construction practices have been implemented (hot taps on large water mains and looping dead end lines) to reduce water losses due to flushing.
• The city's water meter maintenance program will be expanded to include checking and calibration of all large meters (one and one-half (1½ in. and larger) and the large meters at the water sources. Residential meters will be automatically replaced whenever readings begin to vary unaccountably or do not register within the expected range.
• The city will continue to maintain monthly records reflecting the difference between water production and metered sales. The city will then take additional steps to identify and eliminate the source or sources of system losses.
• The city water system maps showing the location and size of all lines, valves, and hydrants will be periodically updated as new mains are added and as information is discovered during repair or replacement operations.
• The city will continue to evaluate all water service meters to insure they are adequately sized for the average and peak flow rates. Meters that are inadequately sized will be replaced with the recommended meter sizes.
• The storage tanks are observed continually for evidence of overflowing. Automatic level controlled equipment will be kept in proper calibration by routine maintenance.
• The city has raw and finished water metering at all sources for water.
• In order to promote water conservation, the city will continue to update local building codes to require all plumbing fixtures and piping in new construction be sized in accordance with the State Plumbing Code and Georgia Water Conservation Law, Code Section 8-2-1 et seq.; the city will continue the current practice of metering all water services and requiring a separate meter for each dwelling unit; and, the city will continue the current practice of utilizing the same uniform unit rate per one thousand (1,000) gallons for all water usage above the monthly minimum. No discount is given for larger water customers. The rate structure is strictly on a "flat" basis. No discount is given for irrigation water meters.

1226: The boundaries and designations of the districts provided for herein are hereby established as shown on the map identified by the title "Zoning Map of LaFayette, Georgia," and the signature of the Mayor of LaFayette and attested by the City Manager. The Zoning Map, together with all explanatory matter thereon, is hereby adopted and made a part of this Chapter. The original of this Map shall be filed in the office of the City Manager and shall show thereon the date of its adoption and of subsequent amendments.
1227:
When there is uncertainty as to the boundary of any district as shown on the Zoning Map adopted herein, the following rules shall apply:
(1) Where district boundary lines are shown as approximately following the centerlines of streets, alleys, highways, streams, lakes, or easements, or the boundary lines of streets, alleys, highways, lot lines, land lot lines, or civil boundaries, such lines shall be construed to be such boundaries.
(2) Where district boundary lines are shown approximately parallel to the centerlines or right-of-way lines of streets, alleys or highways, such district boundary lines shall be construed as being parallel thereto and at such distance therefrom as indicated on the Zoning Map. If no distance is given, the distance may be determined by the scale of the Map.
(3) Where a lot held in one ownership and of record at the effective date of this Chapter is divided by a district boundary line, the entire lot shall be construed to be within the less restrictive district, provided that such extension shall not include any part of such lot more than forty (40) feet beyond the district boundary line.
(4) Where property is hereafter annexed and not zoned upon annexation, it is hereby declared R-1 Residential.
1229:
The regulations set by this Chapter within each district shall be minimum regulations and shall apply uniformly to each class, type or use of building or land, except as hereinafter provided.

1230: No building or land shall hereafter be used or occupied and no building or part thereof shall hereafter be erected, constructed, reconstructed, structurally altered or moved unless in conformity with all the regulations herein specified for the district in which it is located.
1231: No building or other structure shall hereafter be created or altered to exceed the height, or to have a greater number of families or occupy a smaller lot area per family, or occupy a greater percentage of lot area than herein required; or in any other manner contrary to the provisions of this Chapter.
1232: No lot, even though it may consist of one or more adjacent lots of record, shall be reduced in size so that the lot width or depth, front, side or rear yard, lot area per family, or other requirements of this Chapter, are not maintained. This section shall not apply when a portion of a lot is subsequently acquired for public purposes.
1233: No building hereafter shall be erected except on a lot as defined herein, and in no case shall there be more than one (1) principal building on each lot except as otherwise provided herein.
1234:
No building shall be erected on a lot without direct access to a public street, and no lot shall be created which does not abut for at least 25 feet along a public street. With regard to only lots located in B-1 and B-2 Districts that do not have a direct access to a public street, the requirements of this Subsection may be satisfied if any such lot has a perpetual non-exclusive easement at least 25 feet in width for the purposes of ingress, egress, and utilities extending from said lot to a public street.
